title: Protoplast Method for Chromosome Preparation with Zymoseptoria tritici
author: Pat Martinez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.s25egg6

steps.title: Culture Zymoseptoria tritici
steps.instruction: Grow single-spore isolate in 40 ml yeast-sucrose broth (without chloramphenicol) until cells are in log phase.

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 5-8 days at room temperature in a shaker at 150-200 rpm.
Ensure cells do not grow past log phase to facilitate protoplast formation.

steps.title: Harvest and Wash Cells
steps.instruction: Harvest the spores and mycelium and perform an initial wash.

substeps.instruction: Transfer culture to a sterile 50 ml Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at top speed in an IEC clinical centrifuge for 5 minutes.
Pour off the supernatant.
Add 40 ml of sterile 600 mM MgSO4 (pH 5.8) and resuspend cells completely.
Centrifuge again at top speed for 5 minutes in an IEC clinical centrifuge to harvest washed cells.

steps.title: Prepare Protoplasts
steps.instruction: Digest cell walls using Novozyme 234 in a magnesium sulfate solution.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a filter-sterilized solution of 1.2 M MgSO4 (pH 5.8) containing 3.0 mg/ml Novozyme 234 by mixing and forcing slowly through a 5 ml syringe-mounted Nalgene filter.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 20 ml of this Novozyme solution.
Transfer the mixture to a 40 ml glass Corex centrifuge tube.
Incubate at 30 °C for 2 hours without agitation.
Check for protoplast formation after 2 hours, then every 15 minutes, avoiding unnecessary agitation.

steps.title: Isolate and Wash Protoplasts
steps.instruction: Separate protoplasts from the digestion liquid and wash them with sorbitol.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge in an IEC clinical centrifuge at top speed for 3 minutes.
Pipette away the cloudy brown liquid from the bottom, saving the top layer of pinkish cells (protoplasts and undigested spores).
Add 20 ml of 1.2 M sorbitol, resuspend cells, and centrifuge at top speed in an IEC clinical centrifuge for 5 minutes.
Discard supernatant and save the pellet; repeat this wash step once more (two washes total).

steps.title: Quantify and Adjust Protoplast Concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the concentration of protoplasts and adjust to the target density.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend protoplasts in 0.4 ml of 1.0 M sorbitol.
Quantify concentration using a hemocytometer (a 1:10 dilution may be required).
Add 1.2 M sorbitol to achieve a final concentration of 5-10 x 10^8 protoplasts per ml.

steps.title: Embed Protoplasts in Agarose Plugs
steps.instruction: Embed the protoplasts in low melting point (LMP) agarose and solidify them into plugs.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of 2.2% LMP agarose (in TE) to the protoplasts and mix gently.
Keep the solution liquid in a 37 °C water bath.
Tape closed one end of plug molds.
Using a pasteur pipette, fill each well of the plug mold by pushing the pipette to the bottom and working upward.
Allow plugs to solidify for two hours at 4 °C.

steps.title: Lyse Cells in Plugs
steps.instruction: Lysis of the embedded cells using a lysis buffer.

substeps.instruction: Push plugs out using a flame-blunted pasteur pipette into a 15 ml Falcon tube containing 10 ml lysis buffer (1% sarkosyl, 450 mM EDTA, 1 mg/ml proteinase K).
Incubate tubes at 50 °C for 48 hours.
Replace the lysis buffer once after the first 24 hours.

steps.title: Rinse and Store Plugs
steps.instruction: Perform final rinse and storage of the plugs.

substeps.instruction: Rinse plugs in 500 mM EDTA.
Store plugs in 500 mM EDTA at 4 °C.
